surface_mechanism_description: Self-limiting Ga deposition is achieved through the desorption of CH3Ga, which provides negative feedback to stabilize Ga coverage. The desorption rate of CH3Ga balances the Ga flux, leading to a self-limiting coverage. The desorption of CH3 from TMGa results in Ga deposition, while the desorption of CH3Ga removes Ga, creating a flux balance.
evidence: The surface chemistry can be summarized qualitatively by the following equations for the surface coverages of Ga and CH3 respectively: d[Ga]/dt = /BSo(1 - c~[CH3]) -/~[CH3]f(Ga), d[CH3]/dt = 3IBso(1 - c~[CH3]) - k[CH3] -/~[CH3]f(Ga). The desorption of CH3Ga provides negative feedback by which the Ga coverage is stabilized to a self-limiting value. The desorption of CH3 of the adsorbed TMGa on the surface results in the deposition of Ga, while the desorption of CH3Ga causes the removal of Ga.
